assign.outcome:
**A Demo tab on Panel — twelve small workspaces, each a recorded guide beside a fresh one to follow along on.** Reuses Doc's own child-tab mechanism for the top tab and its member-page rail (`div.c("page doc-section", () => this.tabs().ac("vertical"))`) for the inner nav — no second nav mechanism invented.

Order, per the owner's live steer: flex from scratch and grid from scratch lead (`display` → `cells` template → the words that apply), then split · add a column/row · resize a seam · fill/hug/fixed · document mode · swap content · roll a layout · drag a panel · close/absorb · the scrubber itself.

![demo 7 — document mode](demo-7-document-mode.png)
![demo 12 — the scrubber itself](demo-12-scrubber.png)

**`flow.js` gained one door, not two:** `attach(root, $root, { steps })` — `record(root, $root)` (workspace.js's hook) is now the zero-option case of it. Given `steps` (an earlier `flow.save()`), it reuses whatever flow is already on that root rather than binding a second listener set, sets `recording: false`, and jumps to the newest frame — the guide pane scrubs forever and never adds a step; the follow-along pane is a plain `panel()` call and records exactly as always. One signature a future `Workspace` class can call too, per the owner's ask mid-task.

**Proven headless at 1280, all twelve:** zero console errors; each scrubber shows N/N matching its recorded flow; stepping to 1 then forward ×3 changes the panel count on the five demos that add or remove one; on "Split a panel", the right pane starts at 1 panel and a real edge-click split there took the RIGHT recorder 0→1 while the LEFT stayed put — separate recorders, proven.

**Two bugs the owner caught live, fixed:** the `pad wash` pane wrapper had no `flex-1`, so `.panel-workspace` measured 0px wide — invisible panels. A missing flow file now checks `r.ok` before parsing, so an unrecorded demo reads "Flow not recorded yet.", never a console `SyntaxError`.

**Found, not obvious going in:** `Flow.mounted` is document-wide, and a busy SPA (every ancestor Doc tab's own hidden-but-mounted preview panels) keeps rewriting it — a headless driver racing that array can miss its own flow entirely. Worked around in `demo/page.js` by stashing the flow straight on its own element (`.el.flow`), independent of the array; `Flow.mounted` itself is unchanged and still the documented door for everything else.

**Left:** demo 7's screenshot shows mostly the RIGHT pane clearly — the LEFT's document-mode content is real (3 panels, confirmed via DOM) but scrolls past the 20em pane at this screenshot's scroll position, a cosmetic gap not a functional one. No named preset in the "roll a layout" demo (dice only) — the drawer's preset picker was skipped to keep every pane self-contained (no shared global drawer between two side-by-side workspaces).

**Follow-up landed — panels now read as boxes, not seam lines.** `demo/page.js` only, three fixes: (1) the demo row now wears `.ac("bleed")`, claiming the pages full grid width instead of sitting in `main`; (2) every leaf defaults to `tone: "surface"` and every leafs `.panel-workspace` now carries an explicit `border: 1px solid var(--line)` (tone alone paints nothing on a scene template — checked templates.js, only the 15 section bands read it); (3) the seven structure demos (split, add-column-row, resize-seam, document-mode, drag-panel, close-absorb, scrubber-itself) swap their blank leaves for `template: "rail"` — a real bordered list, not a checkered scene — both in the seeds and re-patched into the recorded flows/*.json so the guide pane matches. Re-shot demo-7-document-mode.png and demo-1-flex-scratch.png; zero console errors on both, both panel-workspace boxes now show a real border.

**Left short of target, reported honestly:** each pane measures roughly 190 to 220px at 1280, not the requested 480px or more. Bleed correctly claims this pages own full grid track (about 491px total, confirmed via computed grid-template-columns), but that track is already reduced by two nested rails ahead of it — the apps own sidebar and this Demo tabs own inner left nav — leaving well under the 960px two 480px panes plus a gap would need. Forcing min-width 480px on each pane was tried and reverted: at about 491px available it overflows to a second row and hides the right pane entirely, a worse outcome than the narrow-but-correct layout shipped. Widening further needs surgery outside this fence (collapsing the inner rail on this tab, or a different split), flagged rather than attempted blind.

**Wrap, not force — the third pass.** Replaced `.flex.gap` on the demo row with `.flex.gap.auto` plus `--column: 24em`, dropped the `flex-1`/min-width hacks on the two panes (framework.css's `.flex.auto > *` rule already gives each child `flex: var(--grow,1) 1 calc(var(--column) * var(--grow,1)); min-width: 0`), kept `bleed`.

**Proven headless, zero console errors throughout:**
- **1280** — two rows (guide over follow-along), each pane **461.7px** wide (target: ≥440px).
- **1920** — one row (side by side), each pane **436px** wide — narrower than at 1280 despite the bigger viewport, because the app's own sidebar and this tab's inner nav rail both scale with viewport too (clamp()-based gutters, an 18%-wide rail), eating more of the extra space than the row gets. Still one row as asked, reported as measured rather than assumed.

Re-shot `demo-7-document-mode.png` and `demo-1-flex-scratch.png` at 1280, both now show a real bordered pane on top and bottom, no width games.
